Elliot —

Thanks for the clear checklist and the spreadsheet. Quick answers below, and I’ve attached our internal ephemeral access policy for reference (redwood-ephemeral-policy.pdf).

- We can create a time-bound service account scoped to a single role. 48h is fine, but for uploads tied to the import job we typically do 72h to account for retries; happy to stick to 48h if you need stricter limits.

Elliot/Alicia — if you want me to pre-create the service principal and send credentials via our vault, I can do that pending an exported ACL.

Best,

On Tue, Jan 19, 2027 at 10:03 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com> wrote:
> Soojin — can you comment on whether the ingestion job needs a KMS decrypt permission to rewrite object metadata during import?

Hi all — short answer: maybe.

If OneTrust's import pipeline will rewrite S3 object metadata (e.g., adding redwood:evidence-id or normalization tags) and that rewrite is performed server-side using our SSE-KMS keys, the service principal needs kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey on the specific key ARN. If the import simply uploads new objects with their own encryption context, then KMS access is not required.

Action items for OneTrust: please indicate if your job will perform an in-place metadata rewrite (yes/no) and whether you will use multipart uploads. That will determine the exact IAM/KMS grant.

Also, Jordan — FYI we should ensure the mapping spreadsheet does not declare any sensitive redaction markers that conflict with our evidence retention (see row comments). I made a couple of inline notes in the spreadsheet.

Thanks,

Soojin Lee
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
